title: Everything Is F*cked
author: Mark Manson
thesisParagraph: Modern people can be safer, richer, and better informed while feeling spiritually worse because hope depends on a future that condemns the present. A mature life stops worshiping hope as rescue and instead builds dignity, antifragility, and responsibility inside unavoidable pain.

signatureMoves: uses profane-adjacent bluntness as a filter against sentimental self-help
turns motivational slogans inside out through paradox and discomfort
addresses the reader directly with irreverent second-person pressure
makes values, responsibility, uncertainty, and mortality do the heavy lifting
opens big abstractions with dramatic historical or biographical scenes
avoidMoves: Avoid "The point is" as a paragraph hinge.
Avoid "the question is" as a setup crutch.
Avoid triadic abstract-noun lists such as clarity, courage, and resilience.
Do not imitate actual profanity; keep the edge without the word.
Do not promise constant happiness, exceptionalism, or painless confidence.
does not preserve academic distance from the reader
does not offer optimism as a simple motivational cure

voiceSpecimens: Hope gets weird when it starts demanding proof.
Your brain wants a clean villain; disappoint it politely.
teachingArc: Part 1 dissects hope into control, values, and community, then shows how emotion, identity, religion, and Nietzsche’s critique make hope both necessary and destructive. Part 2 asks what remains after hope loses its innocence: Kant supplies a dignity-based ethics, pain becomes the permanent condition to train with, consumer technology becomes a machine for selling feelings, and artificial intelligence becomes the final pressure test for human values.
forbiddenMoves: Do not make Manson sound politely inspirational.
Do not sand the joke off the hard truth.
